blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Computer-use agents have demonstrated strong capabilities in interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions. However, games, with their visually rich worlds and diverse mechanics, remain challenging and offer a demanding next step toward general digital control. Current game-agent learning pipelines often rely on large-scale demonstrations with limited coverage of dynamic game states, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain. We introduce Player-1, a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic experience. We extend the computer-use action space with relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions. For supervised initialization, we fine-tune computer-use models on 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories that pair recorded actions with task instructions and visual reasoning. We construct Player-1-Gym, sixteen synthetic 2D and 3D environments designed around control demands shared across games. Programmatically verifiable rewards and randomized observations and control dynamics support multi-environment reinforcement learning with PPO. The resulting Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B improve MineDojo-300 success over their SFT policies by 27.8 and 17.7 percentage points, respectively. Player-1-9B reaches 38.33% success compared with 12.63% for the strongest evaluated baseline, with further gains over SFT on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld. Further analyses show that broader synthetic environment coverage improves transfer, while the use of composite actions that combine multiple keyboard and mouse inputs increases during RL. We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience substantially improves game control beyond supervised initialization, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

Player-1-9B成功率达到38.33%,而最强评价基线为12.63%,在ViZDoom-10和GameWorld上比SFT进一步增高. 进一步的分析表明,更广泛的合成环境覆盖面可以改善转移,而结合多种键盘和鼠标输入的复合动作在RL期间会增加. 我们表明,从合成经验中学习,大大改善了游戏控制,超出了监督初始化的范围,其收益超越了RL培训套件。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Foundation models have developed broad capabilities in visual understanding, reasoning, and instruction following ( OpenAI, 2024 ; Anthropic, 2025 ; Gemini Team, 2025 ) .
Computer-use agents bring these capabilities to digital interfaces, interpreting screens and executing keyboard and mouse actions ( Wang et al., 2025a ; Bai et al., 2025 ; Lu et al., 2026 ) .
Games offer a demanding next step toward general digital control: their visually complex environments and diverse mechanics require precise, sustained, and concurrent control under dynamic and rapidly changing visual feedback ( Luo et al., 2026a ) .
blocks.zh:
基础模型在视觉理解、推理和教学方面发展了广泛的能力(OpenAI,2024年;Anthropic,2025年;双子座团队,2025年)。
计算机使用代理人将这些能力带到数字界面,解释屏幕和执行键盘和鼠标动作(Wang等人,2025a); Bai等人,2025年;Lu等人,2026年).
游戏为一般数字控制提供了一个要求很高的下一步:其视觉复杂环境和多种力学要求在动态和迅速变化的视觉反馈下进行精确、持续和并行的控制(Luo等人,2026a)。 。 。 。

blocks.en:
Recent game agents learn from large-scale gameplay demonstrations and interactive experience ( Wang et al., 2025b ; Magne et al., 2026 ; SIMA Team, 2025 ; Shi et al., 2026 ) .
Yet demonstrations cover only a limited portion of the states an agent may encounter in open-ended tasks, while scalable environments for interactive training remain difficult to obtain.
Despite differences in appearance and rules, we find that many games share recurring control demands such as precise aiming, sustained movement, and coordinated inputs.
This motivates our central question: Can synthetic experience advance game-control capabilities beyond supervised initialization, with gains that generalize to games outside the RL training suite?

近期的游戏代理从大型游戏游戏演示和互动体验中学习(Wang等人,2025b;Magne等人,2026;SIMA). Team, 2025; Shi等人, 2026 ).
然而,示威只涉及代理人在无限期任务中可能遇到的有限部分州,而互动培训的可扩展环境仍然难以获得。
尽管外观和规则不同,但我们发现,许多游戏都有着相同的经常性控制需求,如精确瞄准,持续移动,协调投入.
这引发了我们的中心问题: 合成体验能否超越监督初始化,将收益概括到RL训练套件外的游戏上?

blocks.en:
Three challenges shape this approach.
First, gameplay demonstrations recorded with heterogeneous input conventions and temporal resolutions must be converted into a shared action space, and paired with task instructions and visual reasoning that reflect the player’s intent.
Second, learning beyond demonstrations requires feedback on states reached by the policy’s own actions, but implementing programmatic rewards across diverse commercial games is difficult to scale.
Third, experience from environments with different control demands, dynamics, and reward scales must be incorporated into a shared policy that generalizes beyond the training suite.
These challenges motivate our supervised initialization from curated demonstrations, followed by learning in controllable synthetic environments with verifiable rewards.

这一办法有三项挑战。
首先,用不同输入常规和时间分辨率记录的游戏游戏演示必须转化为一个共享的行动空间,并配以任务说明和反映玩家意图的视觉推理.
第二,在示范之外学习需要反馈政策本身行动所达到的国家,但是在各种商业游戏中实施方案奖励是难以衡量的。
第三,必须把来自不同控制需求、动态和奖励尺度的环境的经验纳入一项共同政策,将培训套件以外的情况概括起来。
这些挑战促使我们从精心设计的演示中监督地初始化,然后在可控制的合成环境中学习,并获得可核查的回报。

blocks.en:
Our results demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience improves game-control capabilities, with gains extending beyond the RL training suite.
On MineDojo-300, Player-1-9B improves from 10.54% success after SFT to 38.33%, exceeding the strongest evaluated external baseline at 12.63% under our evaluation protocol. The same policy also improves on ViZDoom-10 and GameWorld, both outside the RL training suite.
We summarize our main contributions as follows: • We present Player-1 , a post-training framework that builds on supervised initialization to learn transferable game-control capabilities from synthetic experience .
A shared action space supports relative pointer motion, sustained inputs, and composite actions, while 6,044 curated gameplay trajectories provide supervised initialization for subsequent interactive learning. • We introduce Player-1-Gym , sixteen synthetic 2D and 3D environments designed around recurring control demands across games.
Programmatically verifiable rewards, together with randomized observations and control dynamics, provide diverse experience for multi-environment reinforcement learning beyond demonstrations. • We demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience advances game-control capabilities beyond supervised demonstrations : Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B gain 27.8 and 17.7 pp in MineDojo-300 success, respectively, with further gains on ViZDoom and GameWorld outside the RL training suite.
Further analyses show improved transfer with broader environment coverage and increased composite-action use during RL.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Foundation models provide broad language, reasoning, and multimodal capabilities that underpin general-purpose agents ( OpenAI, 2024 ; Anthropic, 2025 ; Gemini Team, 2025 ; Yang et al., 2025 ) .
Vision-language models (VLMs) connect visual perception with language, supporting scene understanding and spatial grounding ( Bai et al., 2025 ) .
Computer-use agents (CUAs) specialize these capabilities for screenshot-conditioned interaction, using keyboard and mouse actions to complete multi-step tasks ( Hu et al., 2024 ; Qin et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025a ; Lu et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh:
基础模型提供广泛的语言、推理和多模式能力,作为通用制剂的基础(OpenAI,2024;Anthropic,2025;双子团队,2025;Yang等人,2025)。
视觉语言模型(VLMs)将视觉感知与语言连接起来,支持场景理解和空间定位(Bai等人,2025年) .
计算机使用代理(CUAs)专门将这些能力用于截图条件交互,使用键盘和鼠标动作完成多步任务(Hu等人,2024年;秦等人,2025年;Wang等人,2025年a;Lu等人,2026年).

blocks.en:
Game-agent research spans planning-based systems ( Tan et al., 2025b ) , learned visual policies and vision–language–action (VLA) models ( SIMA Team, 2024 ; Tan et al., 2025a ; Li et al., 2025 ; Wang et al., 2025b ; Magne et al., 2026 ; Yue et al., 2026 ) , and joint video–action models ( Guo et al., 2026 ) .
Reinforcement learning further supports self-improvement and long-horizon control ( SIMA Team, 2025 ; Shi et al., 2026 ) .
Most recently, Jev demonstrates low-latency game control through a text-only interface, relying on structured game-state representations rather than screenshot observations ( Almeida, 2026 ) .
Complementary benchmarks evaluate gameplay ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) and agentic game development ( Chi et al., 2026 ; Luo et al., 2026b ) .
Code world models synthesized from rules and trajectories support planning ( Lehrach et al., 2026 ) , while game engine development provides trajectory data for world-model training ( Zhou et al., 2026 ) , connecting game creation to learning ( Luo et al., 2026a ) .

根据规则和轨迹支持规划合成的代码世界模型(Lehrach等人,2026年),而游戏引擎开发为世界模型培训提供了轨迹数据(周等人,2026年),将游戏创作与学习联系起来(Luo等人,2026a年). 。 。 。

blocks.en:
Post-training with verifiable rewards enables agents to learn from the outcomes of their own actions.
Environment-synthesis approaches expand training coverage by constructing interactive tasks with verifiable rewards ( Dong et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026a ) .
Adaptive approaches learn which environments to generate or jointly improve the policy, environment, and reward model ( Liu et al., 2026 ; Wang et al., 2026b ) .
In games, SIMA 2 combines supervised initialization with online RLVR and further demonstrates self-improvement transfer across Genie 3 environments ( SIMA Team, 2025 ) . Player-1 combines supervised initialization with learning from synthetic experience in environments organized around shared control demands, demonstrating game-control gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en:
Player-1 connects supervised initialization with learning from synthetic experience through a shared game-control action space.
We first extend computer-use actions to support dynamic game control, and initialize the policy using curated gameplay demonstrations.
We then optimize the policy across Player-1-Gym ’s synthetic environments using PPO with verifiable rewards.

然后,我们利用PPO优化Player-1-Gym的合成环境,并给予可核查的奖励。

blocks.en: 3.2 Supervised Initialization for Game Control
blocks.zh: 3.2 游戏控制监督初始化

blocks.en:
The extended action space in Section 3.1 defines the available controls, but the policy must learn when and how to use them.
In this section, we describe how we use SFT on a compact collection of curated gameplay demonstrations to initialize computer-use models for subsequent learning from synthetic experience.
blocks.zh:
第3.1节的扩展行动空间界定了现有的控制,但政策必须学习何时以及如何使用这些控制。
在本节中,我们描述了我们如何利用SFT在一个精密的集式游戏游戏演示中,来初始化计算机使用模型,以便日后从合成经验中学习.

blocks.en:
We curate 6,044 gameplay trajectories comprising 295,097 interaction turns from public datasets ( Choi et al., 2026 ; Markov AI, 2026 ; Yue et al., 2026 ; Baker et al., 2022 ) and in-house recordings, mapping recorded controls to the shared game-control action space defined in Section 3.1 .
Controls are aligned to shared action intervals, and source-specific mouse calibration expresses relative inputs in normalized, pixel-equivalent coordinates.
After filtering incomplete or redundant recordings, we use a VLM ( Google DeepMind, 2026 ) to annotate the recorded actions with task instructions and per-turn visual reasoning.
For reasoning annotation, the VLM conditions on the task instruction, current and past observations, and the action target.
Figure 2 illustrates input coverage and an annotated demonstration.
Appendix B details the sources, alignment, calibration, and annotation procedures.
blocks.zh:
我们整理了6,044个游戏游戏轨迹,其中包括来自公共数据集的295,097个交互转折(Choi等人,2026年;Markov AI,2026年;Yue等人,2026年;Baker等人,2022年)和内部录音,将记录控制映射到第3.1节定义的共享游戏控制动作空间.
控制与共享的动作间隔对齐,针对源的鼠标校准在正态,像素等效坐标中表示相对输入.
在过滤不完整或冗余的录音后,我们使用一个VLM(Google DeepMind,2026年),用任务指示和每回合的视觉推理来注释所记录的动作.
为了推理说明,VLM对任务指示,当前和过去的观察,以及行动目标都有条件.
图2显示了投入覆盖面和附加说明的演示。

blocks.en: 3.3 Player-1-Gym : Learning from Synthetic Experience
blocks.zh: 3.3 玩家-1-健身:学习合成经验

blocks.en:
We construct Player-1-Gym , a suite of synthetic environments organized around control demands shared across games.
Programmatically verifiable rewards, together with randomized observations and control dynamics, support our multi-environment PPO training of the SFT-initialized policy.
blocks.zh:
我们构建了Player-1-Gym, 一套围绕控制需求组织的合成环境,
方案可核查的奖励,加上随机观察和控制动态,支持我们对SFT-初始化政策的多环境PPO培训.

blocks.en:
We identify recurring control demands across games and organize training tasks into five families: aiming, combat, driving, navigation, and UI interaction.
For example, aiming tasks require pointer-based or camera-relative target tracking, while combat tasks combine movement with attack timing.
Building upon our own shared 2D and 3D engines, reusable assets, and scene templates, we implement sixteen environments that require these forms of control through different game mechanics, viewpoints, and spatial layouts, as shown in Figure 3 (a–b).
A unified runtime provides screenshot observations and executes the shared game-control action space.
This shared foundation facilitates extending the suite with new environments while maintaining consistent observation and action interfaces.
blocks.zh:
我们确定所有游戏中反复出现的控制需求,并将培训任务组织到五个家庭:目标、战斗、驾驶、导航和UI互动。
例如,瞄准任务需要基于指针或相机相对的目标跟踪,而战斗任务则将移动与攻击时间相结合.
在我们自己共享的2D和3D引擎、可重复使用的资产和场景模板的基础上,我们通过不同的游戏力学、观点和空间布局,实施16个需要这些控制形式的环境,如图3(a-b)所示。
统一的运行时间提供截图观察,并执行共享的游戏控制动作空间.
这一共享的基础有助于扩大套间,增加新的环境,同时保持一致的观察和行动界面。

blocks.en:
To provide verifiable training feedback, each environment defines game- and task-specific scoring rules over changing game states.
Score increments supply step-level rewards, providing dense and verifiable feedback without a learned judge, while privileged state is not exposed to the policy.
blocks.zh:
为了提供可核查的训练反馈,每个环境都定义了游戏和任务特定评分规则,而不是改变游戏状态.
积分递增提供阶梯级奖励,在没有有学识的法官的情况下提供密集和可核查的反馈,而特权国家则不受该政策的影响.

To further broaden training experience within each environment, we randomize four complementary dimensions in Player-1-Gym : (1) Appearance : colors, lighting, and assets; (2) Camera : projection, placement, and initial orientation; (3) Scene : layouts, spawns, and task-specific configurations; and (4) Control : input-response gains for camera rotation, movement, driving, and steering where applicable. All four dimensions are jointly randomized during training where supported.
Examples are provided in Figure 3 (c).
Appendix C further specifies the distributions and per-environment settings.

为了进一步扩大每个环境中的训练经验,我们在Player-1-Gym中随机划分四个互补维度: (1) 外观:颜色、照明和资产; (2)相机:投影,放置,以及初始方向; (3)场景:布局,产卵,以及任务特定配置; (4)控制:相机旋转,移动,驾驶,方向方向的输入-响应增益. 在得到支助的培训期间,所有四个层面都是共同随机的。

blocks.en: 4 Experiments
blocks.zh: 4 实验

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup
blocks.zh: 4.1 实验设置

blocks.en:
We initialize Player-1-9B and Player-1-35B-A3B from their respective Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.5-35B-A3B backbones.
Both undergo two epochs of SFT on the full demonstration dataset with action-balanced sampling.
We then apply proximal policy optimization (PPO) in the sixteen-environment Player-1-Gym suite.
Both model sizes train on the full sixteen-environment suite with a budget of 200 RL steps. Each training step collects 256 episodes allocated equally across environments, with at most 50 interaction turns per episode.
More training details and hyperparameters are provided in Appendix D .
blocks.zh:
我们从各自的Quen3.5-9B和Quen3.5-35B-A3B骨干开始初始化Player-1-9B和Player-1-35B-A3B.
两者在完整的演示数据集上都经过两个SFT纪元,带有动作平衡的取样.
然后,我们将近距离政策优化(PPO)应用到16环境玩家-1-健身套房中.
两个模型大小都在全16环境套装上进行训练,预算为200RL阶梯. 每个培训步骤收集了各环境平等分配的256集,每个集最多50个互动回合。
附录D提供了更多的培训细节和超参数。

blocks.en:
Besides in-domain evaluation of sixteen Player-1-Gym environments, we construct two evaluation suites: MineDojo-300, comprising 300 tasks from the MineDojo ( Fan et al., 2022 ) task collection in Minecraft, and ViZDoom-10, comprising ten maps from the twelve available maps in ViZDoom ( Kempka et al., 2016 ) .
We also evaluate browser-game interaction on GameWorld ( Ouyang et al., 2026 ) , covering 170 tasks across 34 games.
Our standardized evaluation protocols use 8 trials per MineDojo task, 50 per ViZDoom map, and 3 per GameWorld task.
Appendix E details benchmark composition, metrics, and budgets.
blocks.zh:
除了对16个Player-1-Gym环境进行域内评价外,我们建造了两个评价套房:MineDojo-300,由MineDojo(Fan等人,2022年)任务集Minecraft的300项任务组成;ViZDoom-10,由ViZDoom(Kempka等人,2016年)的12个可用地图组成的10个地图组成.
我们还在GameWorld上评价浏览器-游戏交互(Ouyang等人,2026年),涵盖遍及34个游戏的170项任务.
我们的标准化评价协议使用每个MineDojo任务8次试验,每个ViZDoom地图50次,每个GameWorld任务3次.
附 录 E详细列出了基准构成、衡量尺度和预算。

blocks.en:
We compare against game-specific models, including JARVIS-VLA ( Li et al., 2025 ) , NitroGen ( Magne et al., 2026 ) , Open-P2P ( Yue et al., 2026 ) , and GameWAM ( Guo et al., 2026 ) , as well as computer-use models, including UI-TARS-1.5-7B ( ByteDance Seed, 2025 ) and our Qwen3.5 base models.
We keep their native preprocessing and inference procedures across the benchmarks.
We also compare the base models, our SFT-initialized models, and the final Player-1 models to separate the gains from SFT and those from synthetic experience.
blocks.zh:
我们比较了游戏特定模式,包括JARVIS-VLA(Li等人,2025年),NitroGen(Magne等人,2026年),Open-P2P. (Yue等人,2026年),和GameWAM(Guo等人,2026年),以及计算机使用模型,包括UI-TARS-1.5-7B(ByteDance Seed,2025年)和我们的Quen3.5基础模型.
我们保持他们的先验处理和推论程序 跨越基准。
我们还比较了基础模型,我们的SFT初始化模型,以及最终的Player-1模型,以区分SFT和合成经验的所得.

blocks.en: 4.2 Main Results
blocks.zh: 4.2 主要成果

blocks.en:
On MineDojo-300, SFT raises success from 9.21% to 10.54% for 9B and from 7.79% to 23.38% for 35B-A3B.
Interactive learning raises 9B success to 38.33%, a large gain of 27.79 percentage points over SFT.
The number of tasks completed in at least four of eight trials increases from 20 to 136, showing gains in both task coverage and repeatability.

互动学习将9B成功率提高到38.33%,比SFT大增27.79%.
在8项审判中,至少有4项完成的任务从20项增加到136项,表明任务覆盖面和可重复性都有提高。

blocks.en:
The same policy improves performance on external games.
On ViZDoom-10, Player-1-9B increases scaled return from 0.4361 after SFT to 0.6922.
Player-1-35B-A3B achieves an overall scaled return of 0.7236, surpassing GameWAM, the strongest external baseline at 0.3938, by 83.7%.
On GameWorld’s 3 × 170 3\times 170 episodes, progress rises from 31.43% to 34.45%.
Together, these results show that control experience acquired in Player-1-Gym transfers to first-person shooting and distinct browser games, beyond the synthesized environments for RL.
These gains support using synthetic experience to develop transferable control capabilities without reinforcement learning in each target game.

玩家1-35B-A3B的总回报率达到0.7236,超过了GameWAM,最强的外部基线为0.3938,增长83.7%.

这些结果一起表明,Player-1-Gym向第一人称射击游戏和独特的浏览器游戏中获取的控制经验,超出了RL的合成环境.
这些获得的支持利用合成经验来开发可转移的控制能力,而不在每个目标游戏中进行强化学习.

blocks.en: 5.3 Evolution of Action Composition

blocks.en:
Figure 8 shows increased use of composite actions during RL.
Across Player-1-9B’s in-suite validation trajectories, the share of turns with composite actions rises from 64.7% at the start of RL to 85.4% and 93.2% after 50 and 100 RL steps, respectively.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 6 结论

blocks.en:
We presented Player-1 , a post-training framework for learning game control beyond demonstrations through synthetic experience.
Curated gameplay demonstrations initialize computer-use models in a shared game-control action space. Player-1-Gym then provides sixteen synthetic environments organized around shared control demands, with verifiable rewards and randomized observations and control dynamics for multi-environment RL.
Evaluations on MineDojo-300, ViZDoom-10, and GameWorld demonstrate that learning from synthetic experience advances game-control capabilities beyond SFT, with gains that generalize beyond the RL training suite.
Further analyses show improved transfer with larger training suites.
Together, these findings establish synthetic experience as an effective resource for learning transferable game control without online training in each target game.
blocks.zh:
我们介绍了Player-1, 一个通过合成经验学习游戏控制的训练后框架。
奇幻游戏游戏演示在共享游戏控制动作空间中初始化计算机使用模型. Player-1-Gym随后为围绕共享控制需求组织起来的16个合成环境提供了可核查的奖赏以及多环境RL的随机观测和控制动态.
关于MineDojo-300,ViZDoom-10,以及GameWorld的评价表明,从合成经验中学习可以提升游戏控制能力,超越SFT,其收益概括到RL训练套装之外.
进一步的分析显示,随着培训套间扩大,转调工作有所改善。
这些发现共同确立了合成经验,作为在每款目标游戏中不进行在线培训而学习可转移游戏控制的有效资源.

blocks.en: D.1 Supervised Fine-Tuning

blocks.en: For supervised fine-tuning, both model sizes use token-level cross-entropy on the current turn’s reasoning and action, with the history in Appendix A.3 .

blocks.en:
In human gameplay recordings, some actions occupy only a small fraction of playing time but are critical for game progress.
For example, left mouse button inputs account for less than 1% of valid inputs in the original recordings, which are dominated by keyboard inputs and mouse movement.
In addition to selecting and filtering demonstrations for action coverage during data curation, we use action-balanced sampling to strengthen supervision for these infrequent but important actions.
We classify each turn by its current recorded action into overlapping pools: keyboard, mouse movement, click, hold, any mouse button, keyboard–mouse, movement–click, keyboard–click, and keyboard–movement–click.
Keyboard includes held and tapped keys; keyboard–mouse includes any mouse input, including scrolling.
Other contains the remaining turns, including wait and scroll-only actions.
Each draw selects a pool proportionally to its weight (1 for each control pool; 0.1 for Other), then samples a turn uniformly with replacement.

blocks.en: E.1 Baseline Inference and Action Adapters

blocks.en:
We deploy JARVIS-VLA with its action-token decoder and two history entries to predict one action per decision.
UI-TARS-1.5-7B uses three previous screenshots, deterministic decoding, and a 400-token output limit. Its adapter maps pixel-coordinate actions to one benchmark interval, with drag and double-click unsupported.
NitroGen aggregates an 18-action chunk into six benchmark decisions (three native actions per decision), refreshing the image after each chunk.
GameWAM predicts 16 actions and executes eight before replanning, using its Minecraft checkpoint outside Doom and its ViZDoom checkpoint for Doom.
Open-P2P uses visual-only conditioning and session-specific recurrent state.
All temporal inference state is isolated between episodes.

GameWorld includes 170 tasks across 34 diverse browser games. We evaluate our model for three trials with seeds 0, 1, and 2 (Table 12 ).

Action duration, observation geometry, and admissible controls follow each game’s configuration, and multi-role games keep separate histories.
